title: Canaan Landscape Zones
subtitle: Regional geography without false environmental precision
summary: Explore broad landscape zones that shape movement and settlement across the southern Levant. The current visuals are project-authored schematics, not reconstructed ancient vegetation maps.
disclaimer: These are schematic regional environments based on broad geographic distinctions already used by the atlas. They do not claim exact ancient coastlines, field boundaries, vegetation cover, settlement density, or tree-by-tree reconstruction. Scientific paleoenvironment layers require separate source and license verification.

evidenceLegend.label: Schematic landscape
evidenceLegend.description: Project-authored visual shorthand for a broad landscape form; it is not a photograph or measured terrain model.

evidenceLegend.label: Regional interpretation
evidenceLegend.description: A broad historical-geographic interpretation used to explain travel, settlement, and environmental contrast without drawing exact ancient boundaries.

evidenceLegend.label: Environmental uncertainty
evidenceLegend.description: Ancient vegetation, hydrology, shorelines, and land use changed through time and require period-specific scientific evidence.

panorama.alt: A schematic interactive landscape used to compare broad Canaan regional zones; not a photographic or archaeological reconstruction.

comparison.label: Canaan regional landscapes
comparison.intro: Switch among broad landscape zones. The zone names are geographic teaching categories, not a claim that ancient political or ecological boundaries were fixed.

options.label: Central highlands
options.summary: A north-south highland spine forms a major inland setting for many biblical narratives and settlements.
options.rationale: The contrast between uplands and surrounding lowlands is a durable geographic feature useful for explaining travel, visibility, agriculture, and settlement patterns.
options.objections: The schematic does not specify ancient forest cover, terrace extent, rainfall, or settlement density for any particular century.

options.label: Coastal plain
options.summary: The Mediterranean coastal lowlands provide a different travel and settlement environment from the inland highlands.
options.rationale: Broad coastal-lowland geography is secure, while local shorelines, dunes, marshes, and harbors changed through time.
options.objections: No ancient shoreline or harbor position is reconstructed here; modern coastline geometry must not automatically be treated as ancient.

options.label: Jezreel lowlands
options.summary: The Jezreel Valley is a major lowland corridor framed by prominent uplands and repeated biblical conflict settings.
options.rationale: The valley itself is an established physical region. Exact battle deployments and historical route lines remain separate interpretive questions.
options.objections: This schematic does not reproduce measured relief or claim an exact ancient road alignment.

options.label: Jordan Valley
options.summary: The Jordan Rift forms a pronounced north-south depression with distinctive heat, water, and travel conditions.
options.rationale: The valley is a major physical-geographic system that helps explain east-west crossings and north-south movement.
options.objections: River channels, floodplains, wetlands, Dead Sea levels, and agricultural zones changed through time and are not reconstructed here.

options.label: Shephelah
options.summary: Rolling foothills between the coastal plain and Judean highlands create a transition zone repeatedly important in biblical conflict and movement.
options.rationale: The low-hill transition is geographically meaningful even when exact political frontiers changed from period to period.
options.objections: The visual does not assert fixed territorial borders or reconstruct specific valleys, towns, vegetation, or fortification systems.

options.label: Galilean hills
options.summary: Northern hill country and basin systems create a more broken landscape than the major lowland corridors.
options.rationale: Broad upland-lowland relationships are useful for understanding later Galilee as well as earlier northern geography.
options.objections: This is not yet the first-century Galilee reconstruction planned for Batch 5 and does not claim period-specific settlement or vegetation.

options.label: Negev
options.summary: The southern arid and semi-arid zone contrasts strongly with the Mediterranean hill country and lowlands farther north.
options.rationale: The Negev is an established broad region; its aridity and travel constraints are important to biblical geography.
options.objections: Rainfall, grazing capacity, runoff, settlement, and vegetation varied through time. This schematic must not be read as a precise paleoclimate reconstruction.

hotspots.label: Highland spine
hotspots.summary: A schematic reminder that inland uplands form a major north-south landscape axis.

whyShown.evidence: The atlas already treats Canaan as a broad region and repeatedly maps highland locations within it.
whyShown.inference: The drawn ridges are generic teaching geometry rather than measured elevations or an ancient landscape photograph.
whyShown.alternatives: Future verified DEM and paleoenvironment layers should replace the schematic where appropriate.

hotspots.label: Coastal lowland
hotspots.summary: A schematic flat coastal zone used to contrast Mediterranean lowlands with the inland highlands.

whyShown.evidence: The coastal plain is a major physical region in southern Levantine geography.
whyShown.inference: Water and low relief are drawn schematically; no historical shoreline date is implied.
whyShown.alternatives: Period-specific coastal and harbor studies are required before ancient shoreline overlays are added.

hotspots.label: Jezreel corridor
hotspots.summary: A broad lowland passage framed by uplands, represented here without an exact ancient road line.

whyShown.evidence: The Jezreel Valley is an established geographic region and repeated narrative setting.
whyShown.inference: Calling it a corridor summarizes topographic connectivity; this hotspot is not an excavated roadway.
whyShown.alternatives: Future route overlays must distinguish known road segments from reconstructed movement corridors.

hotspots.label: Jordan Rift
hotspots.summary: A schematic valley trough emphasizing the strong elevation contrast of the Jordan system.

whyShown.evidence: The Jordan basin is a major physical-geographic system central to many biblical journeys.
whyShown.inference: The trough and water line are generic visual teaching devices rather than a period-specific river reconstruction.
whyShown.alternatives: Dead Sea level, river-course, wetland, and floodplain reconstructions require scientific period-specific evidence.

hotspots.label: Foothill transition
hotspots.summary: Rolling hills represent the broad transition between lowlands and the Judean highlands.

whyShown.evidence: The Shephelah is a recognizable foothill zone repeatedly relevant to Judah-Philistia geography.
whyShown.inference: The hills are not a reconstruction of a specific valley or battlefield.
whyShown.alternatives: Site-specific scenes should use measured terrain and explicit site evidence.

hotspots.label: Broken hill country
hotspots.summary: Generic hill layers represent the more varied relief of northern Galilee.

whyShown.evidence: Galilee contains uplands, basins, and strong local relief contrasts.
whyShown.inference: This panorama is only a generalized visual vocabulary for that terrain class.
whyShown.alternatives: Batch 5 should replace this with verified terrain around specific Galilee locations.

hotspots.label: Arid southern zone
hotspots.summary: A schematic dry landscape used to communicate broad environmental contrast and travel difficulty.

whyShown.evidence: The Negev is an established arid/semi-arid geographic region and a recurring biblical travel setting.
whyShown.inference: The displayed dryness is generalized; no exact Holocene precipitation or vegetation state is asserted.
whyShown.alternatives: Paleoclimate, runoff, vegetation, and settlement evidence should be added only after source verification.
